description_full: United States Lime & Minerals, Inc. manufactures and supplies lime and limestone products in the United States. It extracts limestone from open-pit quarries and an underground mine, and processes it as pulverized limestone, quicklime, hydrated lime, and lime slurry. The company supplies its products primarily to the construction customers, including highway, road, and building contractors; industrial customers, such as paper and glass manufacturers; environmental customers comprising municipal sanitation and water treatment facilities, and flue gas treatment processes; oil and gas services companies; roof shingle manufacturers; and poultry producers, as well as steel producers. In addition, the company has various royalty interests with respect to oil and gas rights in natural gas wells located in Johnson County, Texas in the Barnett Shale Formation. The company was incorporated in 1950 and is headquartered in Dallas, Texas. United States Lime & Minerals, Inc. is a subsidiary of Inberdon Enterprises Ltd.

financial_summary: United States Lime & Minerals,  is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $3.2B market cap on $373M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 35% against a 9% cost of capital — a 25-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 26%.

The business throws off $102M in free cash flow — roughly 27 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.23× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.3%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 63% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
